note: Selected NOAA OR&R scientific-support incidents. open_date is the notification date; coordinates may be approximate; status is not live.

records.name: Wellhead Oil Spill; Eloi Bay, Louisiana
records.description: On October 13, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) received a National Response Center (NRC) report validating three Marine Pollution Surveillance Reports (MPSRs) that were recently reported in Eloi Bay. A Cox Operating wellhead in the bay is continuously discharging crude oil. Dark oil and sheen is present within the bay. No estimated quantity is available at this time. NOAA's Office of Response and Restoration (OR&R) is providing fate and trajectory estimates. Shoreline impacts from the oil are anticipated.

records.name: East River Lube Oil Spill; Astoria, New York
records.description: In the morning of October 13, 2026, U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Sector New York contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding an estimated 600-gallon release of lube oil into the East River. The release was secured and boom deployed; however, the boom came apart in the recent storm. The USCG requested a trajectory and fate analysis from NOAA, which was provided. The USCG did not see additional sheening post-event, so no additional requests were made.

records.name: Thorne Bay Harbor Mystery Sheen; Thorne Bay, Alaska
records.description: On October 7, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Marine Safety Detachment Ketchikan contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding a mystery sheen in Thorne Bay, Alaska. The Harbor Master reported a sheen near the sea plane dock at the harbor. The source of the sheen is unknown. The USCG is requesting any satellite imagery that may show the extent or origin of the sheen.

records.name: F/V Sultan Adrift; Ketchikan, Alaska
records.description: U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Marine Safety Detachment Ketchikan notified the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding a vessel adrift in Clarence Strait near Ketchikan, Alaska. The vessel was being towed by the F/V Locomotion when the Locomotion lost propulsion, causing its prop to foul with the lines. When Station Ketchikan attached a tow line to the Sultan, the towline connection broke and the tow was dropped. The Sultan's location is unknown. USCG requests support in confirming a drift model of Sultan to confirm the USCG Command Center model.

records.name: Satellite Anomaly off California Coast; San Francisco, California
records.description: On October 5, 2026, possible oil was observed in satellite imagery provided by NOAA NESDIS (National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service). This anomaly is unconfirmed as oil. The slick, estimated to be 12 nautical miles long and 0.4 nautical miles at its widest, is believed to be a possible bilge dump, located approximately 78.7 nautical miles west of San Francisco, California.

records.name: Helicopter Crash off Catalina Island; Avalon, California
records.description: On September 30, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding a helicopter that crashed into the Pacific Ocean 0.2 nautical miles off Pebbly Beach on Catalina Island. Five people were reported to have been aboard the aircraft. Two people have been transported to the hospital. Two deceased persons have been recovered and one person remains missing. Maximum amount of fuel on board is reported to be 131 gallons of Jet-A.  USCG press releases:  October 1, 2026, Coast Guard, Partners Respond to a Helicopter Crash offshore Santa Catalina Island,  https://www.news.uscg.mil/Press-Releases/Article/4615899/coast-guard-partners-respond-to-a-helicopter-crash-offshore-santa-catalina-isla/.  October 2, 2026, UPDATE: Coast Guard ends search offshore Santa Catalina Island, https://www.news.uscg.mil/Press-Releases/Article/4617351/update-coast-guard-ends-search-offshore-santa-catalina-island/.

records.name: F/V Rolfy Sinking in Seward Harbor; Seward, Alaska
records.description: On September 28, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding the sinking of the F/V Rolfy in Seward, Alaska. The 91-foot vessel sank at I-Dock in Seward Harbor. A USCG-contracted salvage team will be refloating and de-fueling the vessel. The USCG requested NOAA's support with Endangered Species Act (ESA) consultation.

records.name: Diesel Spill from Generator; Towson, Maryland
records.description: On the morning of September 26, 2026, an estimated 2,000 gallons of #2 home heating oil spilled from a generator near Towson, Maryland. The spill went into a drainage pipe that discharges into the Long Quarter Branch and then into a reservoir. Spill responders were on-scene late Saturday where containment boom was put into place and a vacuum truck was being utilized. U.S. Coast Guard Sector Baltimore requested a fate analysis of the fuel to understand potential evaporation/dispersion rates. NOAA provided the fate analysis, explanatory notes, and information about how diesel fuel behaves when spilled.

records.name: Vessel Aground at West Island; Antioch, California
records.description: On September 28, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) notified the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding a trawler that had run aground (when a rope was caught in the propeller) on West Island in the San Joaquin River. The vessel has a fuel capacity of 1,000 gallons of diesel but the pilot reported that only 20 gallons were on board. No sheening or discharge has been reported. Salvage options are being explored. USCG Sector San Francisco Bay deployed.

records.name: Plane Crash off Morro Bay; Morro Bay, California
records.description: On the evening of September 22, 2026, a Hunter Hawk jet crashed into the Pacific Ocean near Morro Bay, California. The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC), requesting a trajectory analysis for 977 gallons of JP-5 (Jet Propellant-5). Additional information is unavailable at this time.

records.name: Fishing Vessel Sunk; Los Angeles, California
records.description: On September 22, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) about the commercial fishing vessel LINDA C that hit the Los Angeles breakwall and sank just outside the main channel on Sunday, September 20. No sheening or signs of discharge have been observed. The USCG is evaluating options and requested a worst-case discharge assessment from OR&R. The owner reported 30 gallons of diesel (maximum capacity 300 gallons) and 10 gallons of hydraulic fluid onboard.

records.name: Overturned Hydrogen Tank Truck; Bellingham, Washington
records.description: On the afternoon of September 21, 2026, the OR&R Hazmat Duty Officer received a call from the Duty Officer from the city of Bellingham, Washington about an overturned refrigerated hydrogen tank truck. The worst-case discharge for the incident is 1.6 million cubic feet of ambient hydrogen. Although it was overturned, the tank truck does not have any obvious signs of damage or release. Requested products from OR&R are weather forecast and ALOHA air plume modeling.

records.name: Fishing Vessel Fire off Nantucket, Massachusetts
records.description: On the morning of September 16, 2026, U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Marine Safety Unit Cape Cod contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding a commercial fishing vessel fire south of Nantucket, Massachusetts. No pollution was reported at the time but the USCG was requesting potential trajectory information from NOAA.

records.name: Whittier Pier and Vessel Fire; Whittier, Alaska
records.description: On September 14, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) notified the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding a fire at the cruise ship terminal pier in Whittier, Alaska. The tour boat Klondike Express also caught fire (with no passengers on board); the fire has since been extinguished. All 2,000 gallons of diesel on the Klondike Express have been accounted for and no sheen is reported. The cruise ship Norwegian Jade was docked at the pier and able to depart the area without damage.

records.name: Sheen Detected at Creole Operating Wellhead; Cameron, Louisiana
records.description: On September 8, 2026, discharge of a sheen was noted at a Creole Operating wellhead in West Cameron Block 2. The wellhead is one mile south of the shoreline. At this time, it is unknown if Creole Operating is responding to this spill. NOAA's Emergency Response Division is assisting with weather forecasts and trajectory analysis.

records.name: Mystery Sheens at Eugene Island Block 316; Gulf of America, Louisiana
records.description: NOAA NESDIS (National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service) Satellite Analysis Branch  has been tracking several mystery sheens in Eugene Island Block 316 since early August 2026. The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) and Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) are investigating the source of these sheens, but a source has not yet been identified. NESDIS Satellite Analysis Branch and OR&R's Emergency Response Division are assisting with the investigation.

records.name: Asphalt Spill into Trapper Slough; Stockton, California
records.description: On September 7, 2026, U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Sector San Francisco notified the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) that a tanker truck containing asphalt was involved in a vehicle accident and went off the road into Trapper Slough near Area Contingency Plan region 2-974. An unknown amount of asphalt has been discharged from the tanker truck. An oil spill response organization (OSRO) is enroute. NOAA provided information about the behavior of asphalt products when they are spilled.

records.name: Sunken Vessel at Boat Ramp; Moss Landing, California
records.description: On August 30, 2026, U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Sector San Francisco contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding a sunken vessel in the Moss Landing Harbor District. The vessel is reported to be a 25-foot center console and is currently discharging fuel presumed to be diesel, creating a rainbow sheen approximately 50 X 100 yards. The amount of fuel on board and maximum capacity are currently unknown. The incident is within a quarter mile of two sensitive sites listed in the Area Contingency Plan (3-305 and 3-310). An oil spill response organization (OSRO) is enroute to float and remove the vessel. The USCG has requested a trajectory forecast from NOAA.

records.name: Crude Oil Spill and In-Situ Burn at TPIC; South Pass 24, Pilottown, Louisiana
records.description: On August 27, 2026, U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Sector New Orleans received notification of a crude oil spill from a TPIC (Texas Petroleum Investment Company) 3-inch flowline associated with the SOB 1A well head in block South Pass 24. A reported 150 barrels of crude oil was released into the marsh and adjacent waterway. Containment and cleanup are underway.  An in-situ burn has been proposed. NOAA was requested for onsite and remote support.

records.name: Intermittent Oil Sheen; Flower Garden Banks National Marine Sanctuary, Bright Bank
records.description: On August 25, 2026, U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Marine Safety Unit (MSU) Port Arthur contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding an intermittent oil sheen observed at location WCB-657 (Flower Garden Banks National Marine Sanctuary, Bright Bank). The sheen was first reported on August 6, 2026, and has since generated multiple reports to the National Response Center, as well as Marine Pollution Surveillance Reports (MPSRs) from the Satellite Analysis Branch of NESDIS (National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service). The source of the discharge remains unidentified. Given the sensitive location within a National Marine Sanctuary, the USCG is requesting operational guidance and initiating an Endangered Species Act (ESA) consultation to ensure response actions minimize potential impacts on protected marine resources.

records.name: Trading Bay Mystery Sheen; Western Cook Inlet, Alaska
records.description: On August 24, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) notified the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) of a mystery sheen, and potentially weathered oil, observed in Trading Bay, Cook Inlet, Alaska. The source is unknown, although the oil is in the vicinity of the Platform Spark, a shut-in and abandoned well. The USCG requested assistance preparing a Resources at Risk report. Further requests are likely if the extent of discharge and a source are determined.

records.name: Mysterious Gas Release; Dauphin Island, Alabama
records.description: On August 24, 2026, U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Sector Mobile contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding  a National Response Center report of a mysterious release of gas, causing significant bubbling in Mobile Bay near Dauphin Island, Alabama. The gas has a sulfur-like odor and the release location is near a natural gas pipeline, as indicated in ERMA (Environmental Response Management Application; OR&R's online mapping tool). The SSC is assisting with hazard assessment and identification of potential sources.

records.name: F/V Resolution; Inverness, California
records.description: In the early hours of August 21, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) notified the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) of a fishing vessel floundering off Point Reyes, California. The USCG responded at daylight and found the 58-foot fishing vessel RESOLUTION beached in the tidal zone with a reported 1,000 gallons of diesel fuel on board. Operations to lighter and/or remove the vessel are underway. NOAA is providing a trajectory forecast, resources at risk (ICS-232), and a spot weather forecast.

records.name: Overturned Fuel Truck; Lawrence, New York
records.description: On August 19, 2026, U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Sector New York contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC), requesting a trajectory for an estimated 3,000-gallon gasoline spill from a truck rollover that occurred around 11am in Lawrence, New York. The fuel spill entered a storm drain that lets out into Hook Creek, a tributary into Jamaica Bay. The USCG requested a trajectory for the incident. The NOAA SSC developed a Resources at Risk report through the Environmental Response Management Application (ERMA) and spoke with U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, as well.   Around 11am an estimated 3,000 gallons of gasoline (note initial NRC report was 300, not 3,000 gallons) potentially entered a storm drain that

records.name: Asphalt Fire at Shelly Liquid facility; Toledo, Ohio
records.location: 352 George Hardy Dr, Toledo, OH 43605, USA
records.description: At approximately 4pm local time on August 18, U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Sector Detroit contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding a fire at an industrial facility in Toledo, Ohio, near the mouth of the Maumee River. The SSC determined that EPA Region 5 is responding to a fire at a different facility upriver that involves a 40,000 gallon kerosene tank. The Interagency Modeling and Atmospheric Assessment Center (IMAAC) has issued a model. The USCG is enroute to the incident. Initial information indicates a 3,000 gallon molten sulfur tank is on fire. The SSC is providing spot forecast and hazard information while awaiting further details.

records.name: Diesel Spill in Monterey Bay; Monterey, California
records.description: On August 13, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) notified the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) of a diesel spill in the Breakwater Cove Marina in Monterey, California that produced a sheen of approximately 50' x 50'. The location is near Sensitive Site 3-370-A, identified in the Area Contingency Plan. California Office of Spill Prevention and Response (OSPR) is en route.

records.name: Pollution Surveillance Report off Santa Barbara; Montecito, California
records.description: The NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) for California received a Marine Pollution Surveillance Report (MPSR) for a discharge 7 nautical miles southeast of Santa Barbara, California. The report was categorized as  high confidence and the source appears to be Platform B. The SSC contacted U.S. Coast Guard Marine Safety Detachment Santa Barbara. No other report of the discharge has been made and the USCG is contacting the operator of the facility.

records.name: Mystery Sheen at South Pass 29; Port Eads, Louisiana
records.description: On August 13, 2026, the Satellite Analysis Branch of NESDIS (the National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service) issued a Marine Pollution Surveillance Report (MPSR) for a slick observed in block SOUTH PASS 29. The image was collected on August 12, 2026 at 2358 UTC via RADARSAT2. From the NESDIS report:  Possible oil was observed in satellite imagery. This anomaly is unconfirmed as oil. The possible oil slick was observed in the South Pass area of the Gulf just south of the Louisiana Bird's Foot. It spanned an area that measured approximately 13.5 by 5 nautical miles. The possible slick was comprised of numerous segments that were mostly linear in shape, exhibiting good contrast and well defined edges. This was believed to be associated with a National Response Center report nearby. Due to the factors described above, confidence in this report was medium-high. Winds at the time of the imagery were out of the WSW at approximately 10-15 knots. The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) requested trajectory analysis from NOAA. REPORT MAP/GIS FILES: https://www.ospo.noaa.gov/products/ocean/marinepollution/

records.name: Satellite Detection of Mystery Sheens; Howell Hook, Gulf of America
records.description: The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Sector St Petersburg, Florida inquired about sheens reported by NESDIS (NOAA's satellite office, the National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service) and other observations near the southern extent of their area of responsibility in the Gulf (130 nm WNW of Key West, Florida). The location of these sheens is in the vicinity of two RULET vessels (Remediation of Underwater Legacy Environmental Threats; a database of potentially polluting sunken ships): the Norlindo and the Cudahy. Both vessels were documented as having heavy fuel oil (HFO, or "bunker") onboard. NOAA's Emergency Response Division has coordinated with NESDIS to assess the anomalies and forecast sheen movement and fate and effects of an HFO release that may occur or continue to sheen at the identified location.

records.name: Mendenhall Glacier Flood Outburst 2026; Juneau, Alaska
records.description: A glacial lake outburst has occurred at Suicide Basin on the Mendenhall Glacier. The basin is releasing.  Flooding is expected along Mendenhall Lake and River late Wednesday evening into early Thursday morning. A crest between 16.1 and 16.6 ft in Major Flood Stage is expected between 5 am and 9 am Thursday, 8/13/2026. People living in the potential inundation area (~1,900 residences) are advised to evacuate today (8/12/2026). No NOAA facilities are located in the evacuation area. Previous to this event, the U.S. Coast Guard requested guidance on the fate and trajectory of a worst case discharge of the fuel storage tanks in the inundation zone.

records.name: Tar Balls at Monterey Bay; Pacific Grove, California
records.location: 1809 Sunset Dr, Pacific Grove, CA 93950, USA
records.description: On August 8, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) notified the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) regarding a report of tar balls of varying size along a 100-meter stretch of Spanish Bay, Asilomar Beach. The oil appeared to be quite weathered. The source is unknown, possibly from natural seeps. No additional support is anticipated at this time.

records.name: Disabled Vessel near Elk Horn Slough; Moss Landing, California
records.description: On August 7, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) notified the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) of the 25-foot GRADY WHITE taking on water near Elk Horn Slough. The vessel was under tow and began taking on water and the tow was released. The vessel is reported to have 70 gallons of gasoline on board and is currently sheening. California Office of Spill Prevention and Response (OSPR) is currently on scene. Further efforts to recover the vessel will take place tomorrow.

records.name: Fishing Vessel NEW ST. JOSEPH Sinking; Seattle, Washington
records.description: In the evening of August 6, 2026, Washington State notified the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) for the Northwest of an 82-foot wooden fishing vessel sinking at Fisherman's Terminal in Seattle.  Reports of heavy sheen escaping the spill boom were relayed by U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) and the State On-Scene Coordinator (OSC).  A worst-case discharge of 500+ gallons of diesel and 100 gallons of heavier lube oil is possible. The USCG requested trajectory analysis from NOAA.

records.name: Vessel Sinking in San Joaquin River; Isleton, California
records.location: 841 W Brannan Island Rd, Isleton, CA 95641, USA
records.description: On July 31, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) notified the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) of a 30-foot vessel sinking in the Spindrift Marina in Isleton, California in the Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta. The vessel is currently releasing gasoline, creating a sheen moving downriver. Maximum fuel capacity is reported to be 320 gallons. The USCG is en route. No additional support from NOAA is anticipated.

records.name: Release of Aluminum Phosphide in M/V THORCO LIVA; Port Arthur, Texas
records.description: On July 25, 2026, M/V THORCO LIVA transited to the Port of Port Arthur, Texas with 02 cargo holds contaminated with approximately 200 lbs of improperly applied Aluminum Phosphide as a fumigant. The cargo on this vessel is steel. During offloading operations while in port, the aluminum phosphide reacted with water and resulted in a fire in cargo hold 01. The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) is requesting from OR&R review of the decontamination processes and cleanup endpoints.

records.name: Satellite Image Anomaly off Prince of Wales Island; Gulf of Alaska, Alaska
records.description: The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) received a report from the Canadian Ice Service regarding an anomaly observed on satellite imagery west of Prince of Wales Island in Southeast Alaska. The anomaly is an area of 12.52 km² and 33.73 km long. USCG contacted the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) requesting input from the National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS) as to whether this may be an oil sheen. NESDIS reported that the anomaly is not believed to be an oil spill or otherwise associated with ship-related pollution, as it does not exhibit the characteristics that are used to identify such events. The anomaly appears consistent with a standard vessel wake, rather than an oil discharge.

records.name: Sheen in Silver Bay; Sitka, Alaska
records.description: On July 23, 2026, the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) notified the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) of a sheen from an unknown source in Silver Bay, Sitka, Alaska. The National Response Center report stated a 100-yard sheen; however, the USCG on-scene found a sheen 1.5 miles long with a strong odor. There was heavy fog in the area, which limited the ability to investigate further. The USCG requested any satellite imagery to help identify the sheen source. Additional support may be requested as they assess the situation.

records.name: Anomaly in Norton Sound; Stebbins, Alaska
records.description: On July 20, 2026, the Canadian Ice Service (CIS), using a Radar Satellite Constellation, detected an anomaly in the waters of Norton Sound and notified the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG). They believe it could possibly be an oil spill in the Sound. The anomaly is “well-contrasted against the ocean backscatter,” and approximately 7 km in length. The USCG requested that the NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SSC) contact NOAA National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS) for their assessment of the observation. NESDIS scientists reported that the anomaly's characteristics indicate natural phenomena, such as organic material or algal blooms. They will continue to monitor the satellite imagery over the area to see if the anomaly dissipates or shifts, and they will update OR&R if their opinion changes.
